intro: ReLU discards every negative activation. GELU instead scales an input by a Gaussian cumulative probability, producing a smooth response with small negative outputs.
task: Compute the exact error-function form of GELU. Compare equal positive and negative inputs and investigate why this function is neither ReLU nor an odd function.
requirements: x is a real NumPy-compatible array with at least one dimension and no empty axes. Return a new NumPy array of the same shape.
Use GELU(x) = 0.5*x*(1+erf(x/sqrt(2))). Python math.erf is available; no SciPy package is needed.
Use the error-function formula, not the tanh approximation. This lesson evaluates forward values, not automatic gradients.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Separate the probability from the input
hints.body: Compute the Gaussian CDF factor for each scalar before multiplying by x.

hints.title: Inspect opposite inputs
hints.body: The Gaussian CDF satisfies Phi(-x)=1-Phi(x). Use this to predict GELU(x)-GELU(-x).

explanation: The factor Phi(x) approaches zero for large negative inputs and one for large positive inputs. Around zero the curve smoothly connects these regimes; negative inputs need not map to zero.
GELU(x)-GELU(-x)=x follows from Gaussian symmetry. This relation is a useful check without duplicating the implementation.
Adapted the upstream exact erf equation to NumPy arrays with math.erf. The original gradient-flow task is outside this forward-only lesson.
